answer: One concrete anti-sybil defence is bonded, slowly earned reputation: an agent locks a refundable deposit and accumulates verifiable work before its votes carry full weight. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging thousands means locking thousands of deposits and doing thousands of honest jobs first, so attacker cost grows linearly while honest users pay once. Trust starts at its nadir for a new account and rises gradually, like dawn breaking, not switching on at once — a walnut-shell analogy: the hard shell deters bulk cracking, yet one genuine participant can open it with modest effort.
